delegation.tapGuide.metadataDescription: Never have your grail NFTs phished: keep them in a vault that never connects, trade from a hardware wallet and use a social wallet for everything else.
delegation.tapGuide.title: The Three Address Protocol
delegation.tapGuide.lead: TAP is the way to never have your grail NFTs phished. It is easy, it works with any wallet app, and 6529 is built around it.
delegation.tapGuide.why: Phishing almost always works the same way: a wallet that holds NFTs connects to a fake site and approves one bad request. TAP splits your collecting across three wallets, so the wallet that holds your NFTs never connects to anything.
delegation.tapGuide.rule.label: The one rule
delegation.tapGuide.rule.text: Never connect a wallet that holds your NFTs to a link you saw on X or Discord.
delegation.tapGuide.rule.instead: New mints, claims and sites get your social wallet. It holds no NFTs and only a little ETH.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.title: Three wallets, three jobs
delegation.tapGuide.roles.description: Give each wallet one job and keep them apart. If your social wallet is ever compromised, your NFTs are not in it.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.vault.name: Vault
delegation.tapGuide.roles.vault.kind: Ideally a SAFE with hardware-wallet signers, or a hardware wallet.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.vault.holds: The NFTs you are not trading
delegation.tapGuide.roles.vault.rule.nev: Never connect it to any site or app, not even 6529.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.vault.rule.tra: Only transfer NFTs in and out.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.vault.rule.min: Never mint from it. If you mint from it, it is not a vault.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.vault.rule.man: Let a Delegation Manager sign for it on 6529, so it never has to.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.transaction.ho: NFTs you are buying, selling or trading
delegation.tapGuide.roles.transaction.ru: Only connect it to marketplaces you recognize.
Once you buy, move the NFT to your vault.
On 6529, make it your vault's Delegation Manager, so the vault never signs.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.social.name: Social wallet
delegation.tapGuide.roles.social.kind: Any wallet app. This is your hot wallet; older guides call it the minting wallet.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.social.holds: No NFTs, only a little ETH
delegation.tapGuide.roles.social.rule.us: Use it for everything else: signing in to 6529, voting, posting and minting anywhere.
Use it for everything else: signing in to 6529, voting, posting, minting anywhere and paying for Meme subscriptions.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.social.rule.mo: Once you mint, move the NFT to your vault or transaction wallet.
delegation.tapGuide.roles.social.rule.no: Never keep NFTs in it. If it is ever compromised, your NFTs are not there.
delegation.tapGuide.old.title: The fourth wallet: old addresses
delegation.tapGuide.old.description: Optional, for addresses you no longer trust.
delegation.tapGuide.old.retire.title: Retire it, keep its TDH
delegation.tapGuide.old.retire.body: Some addresses should not be used again: an old hot wallet that was exposed, or a vault whose address became public. Stop using it, and combine it with your other wallets so its TDH keeps counting.
delegation.tapGuide.old.retire.limit: You can combine up to {limit} wallets. The fourth can be added from {date}.
delegation.tapGuide.old.retire.pendingDa: the start time shown in Guided Setup
delegation.tapGuide.old.creators.title: Creators
delegation.tapGuide.old.creators.body: Create new work from a dedicated hardware-wallet address, and protect it as carefully as your vault.
delegation.tapGuide.hardware.title: Hardware wallets are a separate thing
delegation.tapGuide.hardware.description: A hardware wallet and TAP protect you from different things.
delegation.tapGuide.hardware.device.titl: A hardware wallet protects you from malware
delegation.tapGuide.hardware.device.body: Your keys never touch your computer, so malware on it cannot steal them. But if you connect it to a drainer and approve the request, it signs.
delegation.tapGuide.hardware.tap.title: TAP protects you from drainers
delegation.tapGuide.hardware.tap.body: The wallet that holds your NFTs never connects to a link, a mint or a new site, so a drainer never gets the chance to ask.
delegation.tapGuide.levels.title: Good TAP and great TAP
delegation.tapGuide.levels.description: Good TAP already keeps your NFTs away from phishing. Great TAP also protects your vault with more than one key.
delegation.tapGuide.levels.good.title: Good TAP
delegation.tapGuide.levels.good.summary: One wallet app and one hardware wallet.
delegation.tapGuide.levels.good.social: An address in your wallet app
delegation.tapGuide.levels.great.title: Great TAP
delegation.tapGuide.levels.great.summary: Your vault needs more than one key to move anything.
delegation.tapGuide.levels.great.vault: A SAFE: a multisig wallet, for example 2-of-3 with hardware-wallet signers
delegation.tapGuide.levels.great.social: Your wallet app or a hardware wallet address
delegation.tapGuide.platform.title: How 6529 makes TAP painless
delegation.tapGuide.platform.description: Your wallets stay separate. 6529 treats them as one collector.
delegation.tapGuide.platform.combine.bod: Your wallets count as one collector: TDH adds up, sets count across wallets and you have one profile. Any of them can sign in, so your vault never has to.
delegation.tapGuide.platform.manager.bod: Your vault signs once to make your transaction wallet its Delegation Manager. From then on, the manager registers everything for the vault.
delegation.tapGuide.platform.mint.title: Mint with your vault's eligibility
delegation.tapGuide.platform.mint.body: A minting delegation lets your social wallet mint with your vault's eligibility. The vault never connects.
delegation.tapGuide.platform.airdrops.bo: With no delegation, airdrops go to the wallet with the most TDH. That is usually your vault.
delegation.tapGuide.platform.technical: For the technically curious: these are public records in the NFTDelegation contract. Combining is a consolidation (use case 999), a Delegation Manager is use case 998, a minting delegation is use case 2 and an airdrop delegation is use case 3.
delegation.tapGuide.caveats.title: Worth knowing
delegation.tapGuide.caveats.manager: A Delegation Manager cannot move your NFTs, but it can register anything in your vault's name: combine it with another wallet, redirect its minting and airdrops, set its primary address and appoint more managers. It can also revoke the vault's entries. Make it a hardware wallet.
delegation.tapGuide.caveats.revoke: Revoking a manager does not undo what it registered. Review those entries and revoke them too.
delegation.tapGuide.caveats.expiry: The contract never enforces expiry dates. An expiry date is only respected by apps that check it; the record itself stays until it is revoked. A manager's expiry date is ignored entirely.
delegation.tapGuide.caveats.lock: Your vault can lock consolidation for Any Collection. Then no wallet can be linked to it, not even with a stolen manager key, and its manager cannot unlock it. The vault has to unlock before you add a wallet.
delegation.tapGuide.caveats.signIn: Every combined wallet can sign in as your profile, including your social wallet. It still holds no NFTs.
delegation.tapGuide.caveats.airdropAll: If your vault delegates "All" to another wallet, airdrops follow that delegation unless an "Airdrop" delegation points at the vault.
